skill.name: algorithmic-art
skill.description: Generate algorithmic art with p5.js using seeded randomness, philosophy-driven concepts, interactive parameters, and a self-contained viewer template.
skill.summary: Create reproducible p5.js generative art with an interactive seed and parameter viewer.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution and reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline file names, ordinary art vocabulary, CSS variables, and JavaScript RegExp.exec. The confirmed issues are low-severity external network dependencies: p5.js from cdnjs and Google Fonts resources in the template and instructions. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or malicious command execution.

remediation.issue: The viewer template loads p5.js from a third-party CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle p5.js locally or pin the CDN asset with integrity metadata when distribution allows it.

remediation.issue: The viewer template requests Google Fonts resources.
remediation.suggestion: Use local font assets or system font fallbacks for offline use and reduced third-party tracking.

remediation.issue: External resource use is not clearly disclosed to users.
remediation.suggestion: Document that generated viewers may contact cdnjs and Google Fonts unless dependencies are bundled.

content.value_statement: Creative coding workflows can lose focus when concept, parameters, and viewer design are handled separately. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to create reproducible p5.js art with an interactive viewer.
actual_capabilities: Creates a concise algorithmic philosophy before implementation.
Guides self-contained p5.js viewer creation from the included template.
Requires seeded randomness and noise for reproducible variations.
Defines interactive controls for parameters, colors, seed changes, reset, and download.
Provides reusable p5.js structure guidance for parameters, classes, utilities, and export.
Supports variation exploration through seed navigation and optional presets.
limitations: Generated viewers load p5.js and fonts from external URLs unless the template is changed.
Visual quality depends on the model implementing and testing the generated artifact.
The skill provides guidance and templates, not a packaged p5.js framework.
The source template uses Anthropic-styled UI elements that may need branding review.

use_cases.title: Prototype Generative Artwork
use_cases.description: Turn a theme into a philosophy, algorithm, and interactive p5.js viewer with reproducible seeds.

use_cases.title: Build Portfolio Artifacts
use_cases.description: Create browser-ready generative pieces with controls for seed changes, parameters, and image export.

use_cases.title: Teach Parametric Art
use_cases.description: Show how seeded randomness, noise, fields, particles, and sliders shape a computational artwork.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Concept
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new artwork direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an algorithmic art concept about urban rain. Start with the philosophy, then outline the p5.js behavior and controls.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Viewer
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a complete interactive artifact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a self-contained p5.js generative art viewer from the template. Include seed controls, three useful parameters, reset, and download.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Parameters
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to improve an existing generated piece.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this generative art idea and improve the parameter set so each control changes a meaningful visual behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design Variations
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a reproducible series.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a seeded variation system for this concept. Choose strong default seeds and explain how each seed changes the composition.

output_examples.input: Create generative art inspired by tidal erosion.
output_examples.output: A named movement, a short computational philosophy, and a browser-ready viewer with layered noise, flow paths, and seed navigation.

output_examples.input: Make the artwork more calm and less dense.
output_examples.output: A revised parameter plan that lowers particle count, slows movement, softens contrast, and preserves deterministic seed behavior.
A curated seed list with descriptions of each visual variation and guidance for exporting selected PNG images.

best_practices: Start with the philosophy so the algorithm has a clear visual reason.
Keep seed behavior deterministic so users can reproduce every variation.
Test generated HTML in a browser before sharing or publishing it.
anti_patterns: Do not copy a famous artist or living artist style directly.
Do not add random controls that have no visible effect.
Do not remove seed navigation, reset, or download controls from the viewer.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a generative art concept and a self-contained p5.js viewer with interactive controls.

faq.question: Does it create static images only?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on algorithms, parameters, seeds, and interactive browser-based artwork.

faq.question: Can the same artwork be reproduced?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires seeded randomness so the same seed should recreate the same output.

faq.question: Does the viewer need a server?
faq.answer: No. The intended output is a single HTML file that can open in a browser.

faq.question: Does it use external resources?
faq.answer: Yes. The provided template loads p5.js and fonts from external URLs unless you bundle them locally.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
